title: 10 Camtasia Alternatives You Can Try for Free in 2026
summary: Ten Camtasia alternatives you can try for free in 2026, from Tella and OBS Studio to DaVinci Resolve and ScreenFlow, with platforms, free options and what each one does better than Camtasia.
body_markdown:
Camtasia is a popular[screen recorder](https://www.tella.com/blog/how-to-record-your-screen-with-camtasia) and editor, but it isn't the only option, and it isn't free. Here are 10 Camtasia alternatives you can try for free, what each one is best at, and where Camtasia is still the better pick.


## What is the best Camtasia alternative?


For product demos, tutorials and walkthroughs that you share as a link, the best Camtasia alternative is Tella: it records your screen and camera, cuts silences and filler words, adds auto zooms and gives you a share link. If you want something free, use OBS Studio to record and DaVinci Resolve, Shotcut or Kdenlive to edit. On a Mac, ScreenFlow is the closest one-app match for Camtasia.


## Quick comparison


Checked on each vendor's site on November 16, 2026.

## Is Camtasia free?


No. You can download the Camtasia Editor and use every editing feature for free, but[exported videos have a watermark](https://www.techsmith.com/camtasia/) until you buy a paid plan. Camtasia is sold as a yearly subscription in four tiers, Starter, Essentials, Create and Pro, and the Camtasia Editor comes with Essentials and up ([TechSmith store](https://www.techsmith.com/store/camtasia) , checked November 16, 2026). It runs on macOS 14 or later and Windows 10 and 11.


## Why look for a Camtasia alternative?


- **You don't want a yearly subscription.** Seven tools on this list are free to use.
- **You record more than you edit.** Camtasia is built around a timeline editor. If most of your videos are demos or walkthroughs, a recorder that edits for you and shares a link is faster.
- **You need Linux.** Camtasia has no Linux version. OBS Studio, Kdenlive, Shotcut, OpenShot and DaVinci Resolve do.


Camtasia is still a good pick if you make training content that needs quizzes and SCORM export for a learning management system.


## 1. Tella


[Tella](https://www.tella.com/alternatives/camtasia) is a screen recorder for product demos, tutorials and async video. You record your screen and camera, Tella can edit each new recording for you, and you share it as a link or export it.


### Key features


- Record your screen and camera with the[Mac app](https://www.tella.com/mac) , the[Windows app](https://www.tella.com/windows) (beta), the[Chrome extension](https://www.tella.com/features/chrome-extension-recorder) or the[web recorder](https://www.tella.com/features/online-video-recorder) , in up to 4K
- [Auto Cut](https://www.tella.com/auto-cut) removes silences, filler words and mistakes
- [Auto zooms](https://www.tella.com/features/zoom) follow your clicks
- [Custom backgrounds](https://www.tella.com/features/custom-backgrounds) and layouts for your camera and screen
- [Share links](https://www.tella.com/features/share-link) and an[embeddable player](https://www.tella.com/features/embeddable-video-player)
- [Automated subtitles](https://www.tella.com/features/automated-subtitles)


### Pricing


Tella has no free plan. Every new workspace gets a 7-day free trial of Pro with no credit card. During the trial, clips are capped at 2 hours and exports are HD at 30 FPS. Pro costs $13 per user per month billed annually ($26 monthly), and Premium costs $19 per user per month billed annually ($39 monthly). See[pricing](https://www.tella.com/pricing) .


**Best for** : Founders, product teams and creators who record demos, tutorials and walkthroughs and share them as a link.


## 2. OBS Studio


[OBS Studio](https://obsproject.com/) is free, open-source software for recording your screen and live streaming. It runs on Windows 10 and 11, macOS 13 or later, and Linux. It records well but has no editor, so you need a second app to cut your video. See our list of[OBS alternatives](https://www.tella.com/blog/10-obs-alternatives-you-can-try-for-free) if it feels too technical.


### Key features


- Scenes that mix window captures, webcams, images, text and browser windows
- Audio mixer with noise suppression and noise gate filters
- VST plugin support, plus an API for plugins and scripts
- Hotkeys for nearly every action, and live streaming to most platforms


### Pricing


Free.


**Best for** : Gamers, streamers and anyone who wants a free recorder and doesn't mind setting it up.


## 3. Movavi Screen Recorder


[Movavi Screen Recorder](https://www.movavi.com/screen-recorder/) records your screen, webcam, system audio and microphone on Windows and macOS 12 or later. It has scheduled recordings and simple trimming.


### Key features


- Record a full screen, a window or an area
- Webcam capture alongside the screen
- Scheduled recordings
- Show your keystrokes and mouse


### Pricing


Paid, with a 7-day trial. Trial exports have a watermark. Movavi sells the Screen Recorder on its own or with the Movavi Video Editor ([Movavi store](https://www.movavi.com/store.html) ).


**Best for** : Recording online calls, lessons and webinars.


## 4. Kdenlive


[Kdenlive](https://kdenlive.org/) is a free, open-source video editor from KDE that works on Linux, Windows, macOS and BSD. It's an editor, not a recorder, so pair it with OBS Studio.


### Key features


- Multicam and 3-point editing on a non-linear timeline
- Hundreds of audio and video effects, animated with keyframes
- LUTs, color correction and scopes
- Subtitles with automatic transcription


### Pricing


Free.


**Best for** : People who want a free editor with a full timeline.


## 5. Shotcut


[Shotcut](https://shotcut.org/) is a free, open-source, cross-platform video editor for Windows, Mac and Linux. Like Kdenlive, it edits video but doesn't record your screen.


### Key features


- Multitrack timeline with thumbnails and waveforms
- Runs as a portable app from an external drive
- Chroma key ([green screen](https://www.tella.com/blog/when-was-green-screen-invented) ) filters
- Doesn't rely on system codecs


### Pricing


Free.


**Best for** : Personal and simple professional edits on any computer.


## 6. DaVinci Resolve


[DaVinci Resolve](https://www.blackmagicdesign.com/products/davinciresolve) combines editing, color, visual effects and audio in one app for Windows, Mac and Linux. The free version handles most formats in resolutions up to Ultra HD at up to 60 FPS. The paid DaVinci Resolve Studio adds more GPU-accelerated effects and features.


### Key features


- Professional color grading
- Fusion visual effects and motion graphics
- Fairlight audio editing
- Multi-user collaboration


### Pricing


Free version, or buy DaVinci Resolve Studio for more features.


**Best for** : Editors who want professional tools for free and have time to learn them.


## 7. OpenShot


[OpenShot](https://www.openshot.org/) is a free, open-source video editor for Linux, Mac and Windows, with no subscriptions, watermarks or project limits. It's one of the easiest free editors to learn.


### Key features


- Timeline with unlimited tracks and frame-accurate trimming
- Chroma key, blur and other effects you can animate with keyframes
- Color wheels, curves and LUTs
- Audio visualizations


### Pricing


Free.


**Best for** : Beginners who want a free editor.


## 8. ScreenFlow


[ScreenFlow](https://www.telestream.net/screenflow/overview.htm) records and edits screencasts on a Mac. It's built only for Mac (Apple Silicon and Intel), so it isn't an option on Windows. For a closer look, read[Camtasia vs ScreenFlow](https://www.tella.com/blog/camtasia-vs-screenflow) .


### Key features


- Record your screen, camera and microphone together
- Built-in editor with animations and transitions
- Optional stock media library


### Pricing


From $199 on the[Telestream store](https://www.telestream.net/screenflow/store.asp) (checked November 16, 2026). The free trial has no time limit, but exported videos have a watermark.


**Best for** : Mac users who want Camtasia-style recording and editing in one app.


## 9. ShareX


[ShareX](https://getsharex.com/) is a free, open-source screenshot and screen recording tool for Windows. It records video or GIFs of your screen and can upload them for you.


### Key features


- Record the full screen, a window or a region
- Record GIFs
- Annotate screenshots
- Upload to many destinations with custom workflows


### Pricing


Free.


**Best for** : Windows users who need quick recordings and screenshots, not edited videos.


## 10. Free Cam


[Free Cam](https://www.freescreenrecording.com/) is a free screen recorder for Windows from iSpring. It records your screen with voice narration, lets you cut and clean up the recording and uploads it to YouTube, with no watermark and no time limit. It runs on Windows 10, 8 and 7 and saves videos as 720p WMV files.


### Key features


- Record the full screen, an area or a window
- Voice narration and system sound
- Highlight your mouse and add click sounds
- Cut out mistakes and remove background noise


### Pricing


Free.


**Best for** : Teachers and trainers making simple screencasts on Windows.


## Questions people ask


### What is the best alternative to Camtasia?


It depends on what you make. For product demos, tutorials and walkthroughs you share as a link, Tella records your screen and camera, cuts the pauses and adds auto zooms. For a free recorder, use OBS Studio. For free professional editing, use DaVinci Resolve. On a Mac, ScreenFlow is the closest record-and-edit match.


### Is there a free alternative to Camtasia?


Yes. OBS Studio, Kdenlive, Shotcut and OpenShot are free and open source, DaVinci Resolve has a free version, and ShareX and Free Cam are free Windows recorders. Tella, Movavi Screen Recorder and ScreenFlow are paid, with a free trial.


### Is there a Camtasia alternative for Mac?


Tella, ScreenFlow, OBS Studio, DaVinci Resolve, Kdenlive, Shotcut, OpenShot and Movavi Screen Recorder all run on macOS. ScreenFlow is Mac-only.


### Which Camtasia alternative records and edits in one app?


Tella, ScreenFlow and Movavi Screen Recorder record and edit in the same app. OBS Studio, ShareX and Free Cam mainly record, and Kdenlive, Shotcut, OpenShot and DaVinci Resolve mainly edit.


## Final thoughts


Camtasia is a solid tool, especially for training videos with quizzes. But if you want to skip the subscription, a free pair like OBS Studio and DaVinci Resolve covers recording and editing. If you mostly record demos and tutorials, try[Tella](https://www.tella.com/pricing) : it edits as you record and gives you a link to share. For more options, see our guide to the[best screen recording software](https://www.tella.com/blog/best-screen-recording-software) .
